mission: Reconstruct the object and human-remains passports of the Giza Osiris Shaft, especially Level 3 / Chamber I, while separating documented burial evidence, water architecture and Osirian symbolism from any literal Osiris-body claim.

primary_source.citation: Zahi Hawass, The Discovery of the Osiris Shaft at Giza, The Archaeology and Art of Ancient Egypt, ASAE Cahier 36, 2007, pp. 379-397

documented_architecture.location: under the Khafre causeway, approximately midway between the Great Sphinx and Khafre funerary temple

level_3.condition_at_1999_excavation: lowest chamber filled with groundwater and drained for excavation
level_3.architecture: central basalt pseudo-anthropoid sarcophagus in a water-filled emplacement; surviving lower portions of four pillars
level_3.published_interpretation: Hawass interprets the complex as an Osirian dummy tomb and compares the water-surrounded sarcophagus with the Osireion at Abydos

human_remains.level_2_chamber_C: badly decayed skeletal remains reported inside a granite anthropoid sarcophagus with 26th Dynasty shabtis and pottery
human_remains.level_2_chamber_G: human bones reported near a sarcophagus with Late Period shabtis and pottery
human_remains.level_3_chamber_I: published report states that remains of a skeleton were discovered in the sarcophagus

reported: two schist amulets in the form of Osiris
red polished pottery with white-paint traces stylistically assigned to the 6th Dynasty
level_3_osirian_finds.association_problem: The publication appendix states that amulets and bead were not all discovered in situ; direct association of individual portable finds with the sarcophagus contents must therefore be reconstructed from excavation registers and photographs.

four_pillars_claim.published_statement: Hawass proposes that the four surviving pillar bases may represent four sacred legs of Osiris known in later funerary texts.

relation_to_missing_members_hunt.value: This is the strongest currently identified water-filled Osirian architectural context inside the Giza pyramid complex that also has published human skeletal remains and Osirian/djed objects.
relation_to_missing_members_hunt.promotion_ceiling: It is a biological and ritual control target, not a literal Osiris relic candidate unless independent identity-bearing evidence emerges.
comparison_nodes: Mendes CG53469 / JE35425 and stamped-gold djed
Abydos Djer Tomb O surviving human-material controls

outreach_2026_09_04.target: Egypt Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities / Supreme Council of Antiquities
outreach_2026_09_04.request: current skeletal-remains registration/storage, analyses, Chamber I object passports, GZ.PA.509-517 registers, in-situ status and later groundwater/conservation records

outreach_2026_09_04.target: Peter Der Manuelian / Harvard Giza Project
outreach_2026_09_04.request: Digital Giza archival identifiers for excavation diaries, photographs, object registers, human-remains documentation, plans and later survey records

strong_pass_condition: Recover current object/remains passports and excavation records that establish the exact spatial association, dating and biological classification of the Chamber I skeleton and associated finds.
canonical_formula: FLOODED_CHAMBER -> SARCOPHAGUS -> HUMAN_REMAINS -> OBJECT_ASSOCIATION -> DATE -> BIOLOGICAL_CLASS -> CUSTODY -> ONLY_THEN_IDENTITY
canonical_seal: THE WATER MAKES THE SHAFT AN OSIRIAN ARCHITECTURAL CONTROL; THE SKELETON MAKES IT A BIOLOGICAL PASSPORT PROBLEM. NEITHER FACT NAMES THE DEAD.
